classification.difficultyReason: Recognise semicircular graphs from their equations, sketch the bounded regions and apply circle area formulas.

content.prompt: Sketch a graph of each definite integral, then use an area formula to calculate it.

answer.worked:
The graph $y=\sqrt{16-x^2}$ is the upper semicircle of $x^2+y^2=16$, with radius $4$. The interval $[-4,4]$ covers the whole semicircle above the $x$-axis.
$$\begin{align*}\int_{-4}^{4}\sqrt{16-x^2}\,dx&=\frac12\pi(4)^2\\&=8\pi\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Authored solution sketch of the upper semicircle of radius 4, with the entire region between the curve and x-axis shaded.

answer.worked:
The graph $y=\sqrt{25-x^2}$ is the upper semicircle of $x^2+y^2=25$, with radius $5$. The interval $[-5,0]$ selects a quarter-circle above the $x$-axis.
$$\begin{align*}\int_{-5}^{0}\sqrt{25-x^2}\,dx&=\frac14\pi(5)^2\\&=\frac{25\pi}{4}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Authored solution sketch of the upper semicircle of radius 5, with only the quarter-circle over [-5,0] shaded.
